Hi Tracy,

Thank you for your message and for being candid. I truly appreciate you sharing your perspective, and I want to respond with the same level of transparency and respect.

First, I completely understand your frustration around not seeing the outcomes you were hoping for. That said, I do want to clarify a few key points around the structure of our work together and what was, and was not, fully implemented during our time.

From the beginning, our approach with both Youthtopia and Aesthetic Injector Academy was centered on building a full revenue system, not just running isolated campaigns. That includes CRM setup, consistent biweekly strategy calls, implementation of follow-up systems, and collaboration on execution. Unfortunately, several of these foundational components were never fully put in place or completed.

For Aesthetic Injector Academy specifically, we aligned early on that partnerships, not direct-to-student acquisition, would be the focus. I personally reached out to over 200 practices and organizations in an effort to secure those partnerships. The consistent feedback across the board was a lack of interest in the current offer structure. Based on that, I recommended pivoting to direct-to-consumer acquisition through ads, which is the proven path for education-based offers like AIA. That recommendation was not something you wanted to pursue, which limited our ability to drive enrollments.

Additionally, we made multiple efforts to create higher-leverage opportunities, including introducing AIA to entity["known_celebrity","Viktor Michael","aesthetic injector and trainer"] for a strategic collaboration. We sent three follow-up emails to move that forward but did not receive a response, so that opportunity was not able to develop.

On the Youthtopia side, campaign performance is directly tied to the backend systems and follow-up process. Without a fully implemented CRM, consistent optimization calls, and alignment with your team on conversion strategy, the campaigns alone cannot produce the intended results. Our model is built to fix what happens between the lead and the booked, paying client. Without that full system in place, results will always be limited.

It’s also important to note that as a beta client, you received our program at a significantly reduced investment, with the understanding that this would require close collaboration, testing, and iteration on both sides. The biweekly calls and implementation checkpoints were a critical part of that process, and those were not consistently completed.

Regarding our guarantee, it is structured around achieving revenue outcomes through full implementation of the system. That requires active participation, execution, and alignment across both teams. Without that, we are not able to operate the model as intended.

At this point, I respect your decision to discontinue, and we will absolutely make the transition as smooth as possible. In terms of a refund, given the time, resources, outreach efforts, ad management, and opportunities we pursued and funded (including AmSpa vendor placement), we are not in a position to offer a refund on services rendered.

That said, I genuinely want you to succeed, and I still believe there is significant opportunity within both Youthtopia and AIA with the right structure and direction. If at any point you want to revisit this with full implementation and alignment, I would be open to that conversation.

Please let me know how you would like to handle any final wrap-up items, and we will take care of those promptly.

Wishing you and your team the best moving forward.

Bethany
:::

:::writing{variant="email" id="88427" subject="Re: AIA and Youthtopia Med Spa"}
Hi Tracy,

Thank you for your message and for your honesty. I truly appreciate you sharing your concerns, and I want to respond with the same level of transparency and respect.

I completely understand the frustration around not seeing the outcomes you were expecting. At the same time, I do want to clarify how our model is designed to work and where there were gaps in implementation during our time together.

Our deliverables are not limited to running ads or generating leads. What we provide is a full revenue system that includes sales training, membership and package structuring, partnership and collaboration development, reputation and review engines, event strategy, service and device ROI optimization, KPI tracking, and ongoing operational refinement. These systems are designed to work together to drive revenue growth.

However, these systems were not fully implemented to completion. During our time working together, we completed one biweekly strategy call where we reviewed key areas across marketing, conversion, and operational opportunities. At that time, you had shared that you were in a transition period and did not have the capacity to fully engage in implementation. Following that, we did not have additional consistent check-ins or implementation calls, and no further questions or feedback were raised around deliverables. Based on that cadence, and supported by performance tracking, we were not able to confirm that the systems were being fully implemented on the operational side, particularly in areas like lead follow-up and conversion processes. Without that level of execution and alignment, the systems cannot produce their intended results.

From a performance standpoint, we were able to generate measurable top-of-funnel activity:  
50 leads for Botox  
25 leads for GLP-1  

This confirms that the campaigns were successfully creating interest and bringing new potential patients into your pipeline.

Where the breakdown occurred was in conversion. Generating interest is the first hurdle. Converting that interest into booked, paying clients requires a frictionless booking process and immediate follow-up.

At the time, leads were required to leave the platform, register elsewhere, and enter card details before booking. That level of friction significantly reduces conversion rates. In addition, contactability drops by over 80% when leads are not followed up within the first five minutes. Without a fully implemented follow-up system, including AI automation and structured outreach, those leads will not convert.

We had begun moving toward solving this by implementing follow-up systems to handle booking and reduce reliance on the front desk chasing leads, but due to gaps in communication and missed implementation windows, we were not able to complete that process.

Additionally, Jacques completed and reviewed multiple assets and deliverables to support execution, but there were several extended periods of non-communication that prevented timely implementation and optimization.

For Aesthetic Injector Academy, we aligned early on to focus on partnerships rather than direct-to-student acquisition. I personally reached out to over 200 practices and organizations to pursue those opportunities.  

The consistent feedback was a lack of market interest in the current structure of the offer. Based on that, I recommended shifting toward direct-to-consumer acquisition through ads, which is the proven path for education-based programs like AIA, but that was not a direction you wanted to pursue.

We also made efforts to create higher-level collaboration opportunities, including introducing AIA to Viktor Michael. We sent multiple follow-ups to move that forward but did not receive a response from you, so that opportunity was not able to materialize.

It is also important to note that as a beta client, you were brought in at a significantly reduced investment with the understanding that this would be a collaborative build and implementation process. Our other clients are seeing great success, and we would have loved to implement that fully with you and your team by executing our full program.

Regarding your decision to discontinue, I respect that. However, I do want to set a realistic expectation. The challenge you are experiencing is not uncommon, and it is not isolated to our work together. Any agency you work with will face the same constraint if the backend systems, follow-up speed, and booking process are not fully optimized. This is why most agencies require a minimum three-month commitment, as it takes time to properly implement, test, and optimize each part of the system. There are no shortcuts to building a predictable revenue engine.

Regarding our guarantee, our model is structured so that we continue working until revenue outcomes are achieved. However, that guarantee is contingent upon active participation, communication, and implementation on both sides, as outlined in our agreement.

At this point, we will ensure a smooth transition on any remaining items. In terms of a refund, given the scope of work completed, outreach efforts, ad management, strategic development, and additional investments made on your behalf (including a $1,500 AmSpa vendor placement), we are not in a position to offer a refund on services rendered.

That said, I want to be very clear that I still support AIA and believe in what you have built. I will continue to speak about Aesthetic Injector Academy as a go-to resource for injector education and will continue making introductions and connections where appropriate. You have an incredible course that I truly feel needs to be in every practice and educational class.

If at any point you would like to revisit working together with full implementation and alignment, we would absolutely honor our guarantee and continue working until the intended revenue outcomes are achieved.

Please let me know how you would like to proceed with wrapping up any final items, and we will take care of those promptly.

Wishing you and your team continued success,  
Bethany
:::
